aspects.says: A thread whose flag is already set gets InterruptedException at once from its next wait.
basis: section:A Blocking Call Answers by Throwing, and the Throw Clears the Flag

aspects.says: Future.cancel(true) interrupts the task's thread and marks the Future cancelled at once; whether the task stops before its side effect depends on its own checks, and cancel(false) never interrupts.
basis: section:Cancelling a Future Asks; the Task Decides

aspects.says: A platform thread blocked in classic socket I/O is not woken by an interrupt; closing what it waits on frees it, and that exception means a stop, not a failure.
basis: section:Classic I/O Doesn't Hear an Interrupt: Close What It Waits On

aspects.says: interrupt() only sets a flag; running code stops only at the points where it checks the flag.
basis: section:Interrupting a Thread Sets a Flag, and Running Code Stops Only Where It Looks

aspects.says: Thread.interrupted() clears the flag it reads, so a check that ends inner work can hide the request from the code around it; isInterrupted() only reads.
basis: section:Interrupting a Thread Sets a Flag, and Running Code Stops Only Where It Looks

aspects.says: A cancellation field of the task's own is never set by shutdownNow() or Future.cancel, which set the interrupt flag.
basis: section:Interrupting a Thread Sets a Flag, and Running Code Stops Only Where It Looks

aspects.says: Whoever catches InterruptedException rethrows it, or restores the flag and stops; an empty catch ignores the request and restoring then retrying turns every wait into a spin.
basis: section:Whoever Catches InterruptedException Rethrows It, or Restores It and Stops
section:Spot the Problem: Restoring the Flag and Retrying Turns Every Wait into a Spin

aspects.says: A blocking call answers an interrupt by throwing InterruptedException and clears the flag, so a catch that carries on loses the request.
basis: section:A Blocking Call Answers by Throwing, and the Throw Clears the Flag

aspects.says: On a virtual thread, and on NIO channels, an interrupt closes the socket or channel and the call throws.
basis: section:Classic I/O Doesn't Hear an Interrupt: Close What It Waits On
aspects.reason: the difference shows only by running the same call on two kinds of thread with a real socket; the page shows the run, and the graded runner keeps sockets out of practices

aspects.says: Wrapping InterruptedException in an unchecked exception makes a stop request look like an ordinary failure and loses the flag.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: Restoring the Flag and Retrying Turns Every Wait into a Spin
